title: Can Competition‐Based Programs Promote Conservation in Agriculture? Evidence From the “Most Crop per Drop” Contest
content:
Abstract

This paper evaluates the Arkansas “Most Crop per Drop” Irrigation Yield Contest, a novel competition-based Extension program designed to increase the adoption of Irrigation Water Management (IWM) practices among farmers. We use survey data to classify producers into three categories: contestants, informed non-participants with some connection to the contest, and uninformed non-participants with no knowledge of it. Difference-in-Differences estimates for years before and after the program indicate that contestants applied IWM practices on about four percentage points more of their irrigated land than non-participants who were unaware of the contest, with results robust to matching methods and reclassifying non-contestants based on their proximity to contest fields. Informed non-participants increased IWM adoption by more than two percentage points relative to uninformed peers, providing evidence of meaningful spillover effects from the contest to a broader group of producers.
